title: October 24 — fields, loops and what an observer can recover
summary: Two fresh source reviews join separate branches. ClockfieldRedux advances the clockfield line from homogeneous fixed-ruler tests to a full-complex winding-one vortex: finite-box linear stability and small-noise survival pass, an internal radial breathing mode is measured at tau=0 and 0.1, and none is resolved at tau=0.4. The object’s dimensionless radii and clock ratios vary; fixed outer winding, removed damping and global tau changes limit interpretation. LoopHolonomyNeuron is an independent synthetic ordered-operator observer fixture: late paired internal-reference/return decoding is high while return-only is near chance, and online prediction adapts after a route switch. Its delayed packet, supervised regime maps and known-answer causal intervention do not establish neural holonomy or a biological mechanism. Eromitta’s gradient-screening defect result motivates a future separate test of which screening rule supports defect clocks; it is context, not validation of either new repository. Shared words such as gradient, loop and field are not treated as ancestry.

motifs.title: A field object must supply its own tests of size, time and stability
motifs.description: ClockfieldRedux moves from coefficient-level clock language to a computed complex vortex, then tests its boundary-conditioned stability, measurable radii and candidate internal oscillation. The finite-box defect improves object-level specificity but does not establish isolated matter or a universal geometry.

motifs.title: A hidden route is readable only through an informative measurement
motifs.description: LoopHolonomyNeuron distinguishes paired internal-reference plus return from return-only decoding and includes blind and causal fixture controls. This is a synthetic observability result, not evidence that a neuron computes holonomy.
